text:
alex_sales: Hey team — POC w/ Longview just hit intermittent failures. Browser client gets JSON.parse errors while streaming SSE. Happens ~5-10% of events, looks like truncation mid-object. Any ideas?

maria_engineer: Thanks, alex. Do we have raw logs or a curl replay showing the stream boundaries?

alex_sales: I asked them for logs, they sent this snippet from the browser console: `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` and says the payload sometimes ends with a truncated utf8 sequence like `0xF0 0x9F` (emoji).

kevin_se: That points to chunking boundaries splitting multibyte utf-8 codepoints. If the SSE chunk ends in the middle of a multibyte char, client reconstruction can produce invalid JSON. Which client are they using? native EventSource in Chrome?

alex_sales: Yes, native EventSource in Chrome. They said it fails in their SPA, not in Postman.

jordan_support: Common culprits: intermediate proxy/nginx/Cloudflare buffering, or our runtime flushing in weird sizes. Also check that we set Content-Type: text/event-stream and Transfer-Encoding: chunked and we send proper event delimiters (double newline).

maria_engineer: Agreed. Can we ask them to run a reproduction with curl -N to capture raw bytes? Example I usually send:```bash
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/poc/stream?session=abc" > raw.txt
```Then inspect raw.txt for broken utf8 sequences.

alex_sales: I'll pass that along. They also mentioned a reverse proxy in front of the browser in their infra (Fastly). Could Fastly re-chunk responses?

jordan_support: Yes, CDN/proxy can re-chunk. Also some proxies will buffer until a certain size or until newline sequence. If they re-chunk without regard for utf-8 boundaries it can split codepoints. Workarounds: send small keepalive comments to keep the stream alive and encourage full events in one chunk, or base64-encode payloads (ugly). Better: ensure upstream sets `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `Cache-Control: no-cache`, and disable response buffering in nginx:```nginx
location /poc/stream {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
}
```

kevin_se: Another robust approach: make the client assemble `data:` lines until it sees the blank line that terminates an event, then JSON.parse. The browser EventSource already does that, but if some client-side layer is splitting by tcp chunk rather than event boundaries (rare), they might be using a custom SSE polyfill. Ask them to log raw EventSource `onmessage` lengths vs underlying chunks.

amanda_security: Also flag for security: if they plan to push PII in streaming objects, ensure we have an acceptable data handling note on the security questionnaire. I can prep a short answer for their vendor risk team if needed.

alex_sales: Good to know, they did ask about SOC2 language. I'll loop amanda. Back to the bug — they ran curl -N and attached a raw dump. I looked — there are many `\n\n` boundaries, but some chunks end mid-emoji. Example bytes shown as hex in their paste.

maria_engineer: That confirms it. Short-term mitigation we can recommend to the POC: 1) disable buffering at CDN/proxy layer; 2) add server-side heartbeats/comments every 5s like `:hb\n\n` so proxies flush consistently; 3) ensure our runtime writes whole events in a single write syscall when possible.

jordan_support: To add: check for rate-limiting behavior. If server returns 429 on subsequent calls and closes connection, client libraries might try to reconnect quickly and reassemble partial streams incorrectly. Any rate-limit entries in logs?

alex_sales: Their logs show occasional 429s during load spikes. Could interplay with chunking?

kevin_se: Potentially. If a request hits a rate-limit plugin that injects a 429 chunk, the connection closure could happen mid-event. Suggest they correlate 429 timestamps with parse errors.

maria_engineer: For debugging we can provide a diagnostic endpoint that emits predictable test events with multibyte chars and counters so they can reproduce locally and see if the problem persists when bypassing CDN. I can spin that up on a POC sandbox.

alex_sales: That would be perfect. Could you also include a WebSocket fallback for the POC? Customer asked about that as backup.

maria_engineer: Yes, we can expose a ws fallback. Note: WS avoids SSE parsing issues but requires different client implementation. We'll document steps.

amanda_security: Also confirming: the security questionnaire answer for streaming will include that data-in-transit is encrypted (TLS) and that the stream endpoint supports auth tokens with limited scope. I'll draft and send to alex for the vendor team.

jordan_support: Quick remediation checklist to give the customer: 1) curl -N raw capture; 2) disable proxy buffering (Fastly/Cloudflare config); 3) confirm headers: `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`; 4) server-side heartbeat `:hb\n\n` every 10s; 5) correlate 429s with parse errors; 6) enable WS fallback.

alex_sales: I'll send that checklist and the diagnostic endpoint link once maria has it. Thanks everyone, this is helpful. :thumbsup:

deploy_bot: Deployment started for staging/poc-sse-diagnostics (build #482). ETA ~3m.

maria_engineer: Deployed sandbox endpoint at https://poc-sandbox.redwood.internal/stream-test?case=utf8-emoji — contains controlled events and multi-byte payloads. Alex, share with customer and ask them to test bypassing CDN first.

alex_sales: Shared with Longview support. They're running tests now. I'll update the thread with the curl dump and any further symptoms.

kevin_se: If they still see issues after disabling CDN buffering, ask for a raw tcpdump or we can provide a small client-side polyfill that buffers incomplete utf-8 sequences until the event delimiter. I'll put a reference gist in the thread if needed.

alex_sales: Great — tagging in amanda on security followups. Will report back in a few hours.

amanda_security: Got it. I'll prep the SOC2 blurb and send.

alex_sales: End of thread for now.
